k:audio-multimodal-instructions@1.3:1c6d.excerpt:
## Playback and unavailable content
- If the player fails to load or start, report a tool incident with the task ID.
- A visible waveform with no playback is still a playback/tool incident; the waveform alone does not establish that the recording is silent.
- Do not score unavailable audio as a model-quality failure or make a content-based Quarantine (QN) decision solely because playback is unavailable.
- Capture the browser/error state and whether another clip plays. An old workaround must be checked against the current symptoms; recurrence alone does not establish which fix was tried or why it failed.
- Handling guidance does not confirm that playback has been repaired or that an affected task can be evaluated.

k:audio-multimodal-faq@1.1:c724358c.excerpt:
## Playback and tool issues

### Q: What if the player spins forever or never loads?
Report the task ID and available reproduction details as a tool incident. Do not score the recording as a model-quality failure while it cannot be evaluated.

### Q: Can I use QN because playback is unavailable?
Playback failure alone does not establish a content-based QN reason. Report the tool incident. If other accessible evidence raises a separate content concern, retain it for review rather than assuming what the unavailable audio contains.

## Evidence available at the review
Three batch-05 incident notes describe a player stuck at 00:00 even though the waveform appears. One Trainer reported that a single reload restored playback on A05-P101; two other tasks had not been retested. These notes establish a recurring symptom, not a confirmed cause.

## Suggested advice
A simulated prior Agent 3 card proposed a short alignment note allowing one reload while capturing task IDs and browser state. It did not claim that reload was a repair.

## TL decision
Priya approved a monitored trial for audio_batch_05 only, ending August 28 at 17:00 New York time. Trainers may try one reload, report whether another clip plays, and retain the failed task reference. No content score or QN decision should be inferred from unavailable playback.

Do not repeatedly reload an affected task or mark it submitted without confirmation. Priya requested a short outcome review before extending the trial.

k:audio-multimodal-instructions@1.3:6eeb.excerpt:
## Scoring audio quality
- Assess intelligibility and the affected span, not the word “clipping” alone.
- Brief, localized clipping or static with speech remaining clear is a minor defect.
- An artifact that makes a material speech span unusable is a major defect.
- Continuous artifacts or borderline impact require QA review with timestamps and an intelligibility description. Duration alone does not establish a major defect.
- Before treating silence as a content issue, verify playback, volume, and whether the audio file itself is silent. Preserve uncertainty when this cannot be checked.
